extracted.intended_audience: historical demographers, anthropologists, and historians estimating aboriginal populations (California/San Joaquin Valley)
extracted.subtask_short: estimating aboriginal population, San Joaquin Valley
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and standards for reconstructing pre-contact/early-19th-century aboriginal population totals for the San Joaquin Valley using documentary, mission, ethnographic, and midcentury American sources, with explicit procedures for adjusting and reconciling conflicting estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: By stream densities (stream-mileage/area comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate population by comparing stream mileage and area to analogous regions; use stream density as a proxy for settlement frequency and population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified when ecological territory resembles the comparison area; example: northern Miwok equivalent by stream mileage and area gave 2,480 and 1,535 respectively, averaged to 2,008. Discrepancies may arise from differing stream frequency; take the mean or otherwise reconcile the two measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: By adjusted tribal averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tribal-average population figures adjusted for local conditions (village counts, known tribal structure) to produce an aggregate estimate (e.g., 'By adjusted tribal averages 4,800').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine tribal averages obtained from ethnographers and adjust for known local peculiarities (loss, fragmentation) before summing. The paper lists this as one independent mode of calculation to be compared with others.

rubrics_metrics.name: By baptism data (mission conversion extrapolation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mission baptism (conversion) records and an assumed baptism-to-original-population conversion factor to extrapolate total aboriginal population from recorded baptisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the baptism factor according to exposure to missions/Spanish influence: examples used in the paper include 50% for very exposed delta/bay tribes, 10% for the Cosumnes, intermediate values (20%, 25%) for less-exposed groups, and as low as 7% for tribes that resisted missionization (Moquelumne/Mokelumne). The paper gives explicit baptism counts (e.g., Cuyens 88, Mayemes 91, Apaglamnes 48, Tationes 243 = total 470) and shows applying a 25% factor yields 1,800. Use mission dates and local exposure history to choose an appropriate factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: By extrapolation from American midcentury estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use American-era (mid-19th century) pioneer/government population estimates (censuses, reports, vaccination records), adjust for known biases, and extrapolate backward to estimate original aboriginal population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat pioneer/government figures skeptically (they may be exaggerated). Correct vaccination-based counts for persons missed (example: Ryer's 1,010 corrected to 1,420), then apply an estimated remainder factor (example used: remainder in 1850 represented approximately one-third of original aboriginal population) to infer pre-depletion totals (e.g., corrected 1,420 -> multiply by 3 -> aboriginal value 4,730). Compare multiple American estimates and select/reconcile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple independent estimation modes and average
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive population by several independent methods (stream densities, tribal averages, baptism data, extrapolation from American estimates) and use the mean of results as a working estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper computes four modes for the Moquelumne group (7,200; 4,800; 4,870; 6,000) and takes the mean (5,720) as 'entirely reasonable.' Averaging is used to balance method-specific biases; consider rounding to a plausible whole number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for geographic exposure to Spanish/Mexican influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust expected missionary conversion rates and other contact-related measures according to proximity to expedition routes, rivers, and areas more exposed to Spanish activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: tribes near the San Joaquin River and delta were more exposed and may have higher baptism proportions; lateral-stream tribes less exposed have lower baptism proportions. Use expedition diaries and mission records to assess exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for resistance to missionization and local hostility
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower assumed baptism/conversion factors for groups documented to have strongly resisted missionization or to have been hostile to Spaniards/Americans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper assigns as low as 7% for the Mokelumnes/Moquelumnes due to 'extraordinary tenacity' in resisting missionization; Lakisamni/Taulamnes similarly judged hostile and given low baptism factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct vaccination/voucher-based counts for undercounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust 19th-century vaccination or 'vouchers for vaccination' counts upward to account for persons who missed vaccination or were unrecorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Ryer vaccinated 1,010; after correction for missed vaccinations the paper raises this to 1,420 before applying further extrapolation factors. Apply documented corrections where possible based on the collector's methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use village counts and assume plausible average village sizes when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: When diaries or reports list villages but not population, assume average persons per village (explicitly stated values) to estimate totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: assume 300 persons each for six villages -> 1,800; assume 250 for a cliff village (Taulamne) and extrapolate to others; use conservative estimates where uncertainty is high (e.g., 225 persons each for Tuolumne rancherias). State the assumed per-village figure and justify by comparison to other accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add cautious allowances for unseen or unmentioned settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedition accounts omit villages on certain marches or stretches, add a conservative number to account for likely unreported settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: after Munoz's march upstream from Taulamne the author adds another 500 to account for villages likely present but not mentioned, producing a total of 2,000 for the Stanislaus stretch. Use contextual geographic/ethnographic reasoning to justify additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check and locate villages using expedition diaries and distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify village placements and inter-village distances by comparing expedition distance-notes to maps; use this to assess village counts and spatial distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author compares Viader's leagues-per-leg, chief-names, and locations with Schenck's maps; notes consistency or discrepancies (e.g., Taualames placement on east bank). Use such checks to validate whether named sites were rancherias or transient fishing parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult all available Spanish and Mexican documentary sources exhaustively
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on a single account; examine the full corpus of Spanish and Mexican sources (diaries, expedition reports, mission records) before forming estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's point 1: 'All available information from the Spanish and Mexican sources must be consulted. To confine an argument ... to a single account ... may lead to a false impression.' Use multiple contemporaneous documents to cross-validate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ethnographic reports where mission/spanish data are absent
rubrics_metrics.description: For regions not reached or poorly covered by Spanish/Mission sources, rely on ethnographers (Gifford, Kroeber, Merriam) and comparable-area methods (stream-mileage, area).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the Miwok foothill area was not missionized; the paper relies 'exclusively upon the reports of the ethnographers' and then applies stream/area comparisons to estimate population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limitations of late informants (post-1900/1920)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat accounts from informants reporting after 1900 (especially post-1920) as unreliable for pre-contact/early-19th-century conditions because of dispersal and memory loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's point 2: 'no informants speaking since 1900, and particularly since 1920, can possibly have furnished a true picture of conditions prior to the Spanish invasion.' Prefer contemporaneous documentary sources over late oral recollections for reconstructing early distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account explicitly for depletion between 1800 and 1850 (epidemics, warfare, starvation, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a demographic correction for mortality and population loss due to warfare, massacre, forced conversion, starvation, exposure, and especially epidemics (1830s); quantify depletion when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's point 3: these combined forces 'destroyed in the aggregate fully 75 per cent of the aboriginal population.' Use such depletion estimates to convert midcentury remainders into pre-depletion population estimates; be explicit about the chosen depletion fraction and evidence for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be conservative and explicit when data are fragmentary; prefer stated conservative assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documentary data are fragmentary, make conservative choices for assumed village sizes, added allowances, and baptism factors, and state those assumptions clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout the paper the author chooses intermediate or conservative factors (e.g., 25% baptism for San Joaquin River natives, conservative 225 persons per rancheria for Tuolumne) and explicitly notes where estimates may be inflated or understated. Document uncertainties and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supplementary archival sources (War Department, Office of Indian Affairs, manuscript collections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate unpublished letters, military reports, agency abstracts, and manuscript diaries from archives as additional data points for local counts and tribal presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix abstracts War Dept. and Office of Indian Affairs documents giving counts by river system and tribe (e.g., Fort Miller counts, agency enumerations totaling 2,436). Use such archival counts as inputs or checks, noting their date and possible bias.
